Test Description: This testcase verifies the write-read accessibility of all 52 registers in the MIPI DSI subsystem. The test writes six distinct test patterns to each writable register and reads back the value to confirm correct data retention. The expected read-back value is computed using the write and read masks for each register. Registers that are flagged as non-writable or marked for skipping are excluded from the verification. The test confirms that every writable register correctly accepts and returns data consistent with its defined write and read mask properties.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the write-read failure counter to zero.
2. For each of the six predefined test patterns, perform the following:
   a. Select the current test pattern as the write data.
   b. Iterate over all 52 MIPI DSI subsystem registers.
   c. For each register, check if it is flagged in the skip list; if so, skip it.
   d. For each register, check if its write mask indicates it is non-writable; if so, skip it.
   e. Write the current test pattern to the register.
   f. Read back the register value.
   g. Compute the expected value using the write mask and read mask for the register.
   h. Compare the read-back value against the expected value.
   i. If the values match, record a pass for that register and pattern.
   j. If the values do not match, increment the failure counter and log the mismatch details.
3. After all patterns and registers have been processed, evaluate the overall result.
4. If the failure counter is zero, the test passes; otherwise, the test fails.

Test Description: This testcase verifies the soft reset sequence for the MIPI DSI subsystem. The test reads the current value of the soft reset register to preserve its default state, then writes a predefined reset data value to the soft reset register to assert the soft reset. After a stabilization wait period, the test writes back the original saved value to the soft reset register to de-assert the reset, followed by another stabilization wait period. This confirms that the soft reset assertion and de-assertion sequence can be executed on the MIPI DSI subsystem.

1. Read the current value of the soft reset register and save it as the default value.
2. Write the predefined reset data value to the soft reset register to assert the soft reset.
3. Wait for a stabilization period to allow the soft reset to take effect.
4. Write the previously saved default value back to the soft reset register to de-assert the soft reset.
5. Wait for a stabilization period to allow the subsystem to return to normal operation.
